chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The people will not be upright regarding the obligations (the obligatory shares of inheritance) and divorce, except by the sword.

key_terms.السيف: The sword — metaphor for coercive judicial authority and enforcement power
key_terms.الطلاق: Islamic divorce (talaq), a legal act requiring proper conditions and witnesses
key_terms.الفرائض: Obligatory shares of inheritance as specified in the Quran (fara'id), the plural of farida

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Sadiq say people cannot follow inheritance laws and divorce except by the sword?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) states that without the enforcement of legal authority — symbolized by the sword — people will not comply with the Quranic laws of inheritance (fara'id) and divorce. This statement reflects the Imam's concern about the social and legal chaos of his era, where Umayyad and early Abbasid governance had undermined proper implementation of Islamic jurisprudence. In Shia jurisprudential tradition, 'the sword' here signifies the coercive authority of a just Imam or his appointed jurist, without which legal compliance remains unenforceable.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The people will not be correct upon the Obligations (legislated shares of inheritance) and the divorce, except by the sword’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
People do not behave properly in matters of obligations and divorce without the sword (enforcing authority).’”
